summary: This BCP specifies the approval process for changes to the IANA "IPv6 Address Space" registry and updates RFC 7249.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9812 strengthens the approval process for non-routine changes to the IPv6 Address Space registry. It changes the rule to IETF Review and updates RFC 7249.

subtitle: Changes the approval process for non-routine IPv6 address allocations.

tldr.problem: The IPv6 Address Space registry listed IESG approval for non-routine allocations, but RFC 9812 says a more stringent process is appropriate for major allocations.
tldr.mechanism: The Best Current Practice changes the registry policy to IETF Review, requiring review and community consensus for changes to reserved IPv6 address space.
tldr.outcome: IANA updated the registry, and RFC 9812 updates RFC 7249. The document also clarifies that RFC 1881 belongs to the IETF Stream.

today: RFC 9812 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 7249. It changes the IPv6 Address Space registry policy to IETF Review.

sections.title: Non-Routine IPv6 Allocations
sections.content: Most IPv6 address space is reserved by the IETF for possible future assignment. Occasionally, a non-routine allocation moves address space between IANA registries. RFC 9812 says that major allocations from this reserved space need a stronger approval policy.
sections.plainLanguage: Most IPv6 address space is held in reserve. A major change to that space needs a careful approval process.

sections.title: Changing to IETF Review
sections.content: RFC 9812 replaces the “IESG approval” policy with “IETF Review” for the IPv6 Address Space registry. It says the stricter Standards Action policy is not necessary because some allocations may not require a new protocol standard. IANA updated the registry to IETF Review.
sections.plainLanguage: Changes now require IETF Review rather than IESG approval alone. The RFC does not require every allocation to come with a new protocol standard.

sections.title: Updates to the Registry Record
sections.content: This Best Current Practice updates RFC 7249 to state that future globally unique unicast allocations from the reserved space follow IETF Review. It also clarifies RFC 1881's status: the document was incorrectly listed as Legacy, but belongs to the IETF Stream.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 7249 now records the stronger review rule. RFC 9812 also corrects the classification of RFC 1881.
